About • Collections • Blog • Compare • Privacy Policy • Terms of Service • Submit a pedal • © 2026 PedalFilter Clear Compare ( 0 ) Back Home Vick Audio 73 Ram's Head Back to results Vick Audio 73 Ram's Head Fuzz 1973 Ram's Head Big Muff clone with sweet sustain—3-position mid switch adds tonal flexibility. The 73 Ram's Head is Vick Audio's most acclaimed Big Muff reproduction, faithfully recreating the 1973 Ram's Head variant known for having more dirt than predecessors while maintaining super-sweet sustain. Uses modern transistors with specs matching the originals, hand-soldered through-hole components on US-made PCBs, built in small batches of 2-4 units at a time. Features Volume, Tone, and Sustain controls with a 3-position mid-range switch offering scooped (stock), flat, and boosted mids. This switch addresses the original Big Muff's fixed mid scoop, allowing players to cut through dense mixes or maintain classic scooped tones. Construction includes 3PDT true bypass, Neutrik jacks, and powder-coated enclosure. Requires 9V DC via 2.1mm Boss-style jack (no battery clip). Considered one of the very best Ram's Head reproductions available before Vick Audio's closure in 2023. Vick Audio browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Vick Audio 73 Ram's Head Published on July 3, 2013 Vick Audio fuzz pedal Information My personal favorite of the Big Muff replicas I produce.  The 73 Ram's head is known to be smoother than the 66 Triangle but with more dirt then the Black Russian.  The thing that really sets the 73 Ram's Head apart is the incredible sustain you get with this pedal.  It is designed for the guitarist who wants his ax to sing like a hummingbird, with sweet violin-like sustaining sound.  The sustain control allows you to optimize long sustain with a hint of harmonic distortion.  Hendrix relied on this Big Muff for his smooth, mellow, Electric Lady sound. A switch has been added for three mid-range options scooped (stock) as well as flat and boosted mids.
